newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks wander to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks wander to firmer close.

text.p: Australian shares discounted strong gains made by the Dow to close only marginally firmer on Monday, after bond markets softened on concerns over U.S. inflation and interest rates.
The All Ordinaries index clambered only 3.7 points higher to 2,422.3.

Despite record-breaking runs on U.S. equity markets, brokers said the local market had drifted along in a four point range for most of the day with inflation concerns wiping out potential Dow-inspired gains.

"The market couldn't achieve anything this morning and never looked like doing anything at any stage," said dealer Peter Struk of brokerage Reynolds and Co, pointing to the lack of any clear trend despite moderate volumes.
"There was some switching going on but there wasn't really a lot out there today."
In the leaders, CRA was the only stock to attract attention, its shares sliding 26 cents to close at A$19.30 (US$15.08) as dual-entity partner RTZ dived in the U.K..
With the leaders failing to provide a guide, players looked to the second-tier companies and smaller end of the market for the corporate action.

First to roll the dice was Sydney Harbour Casino, whose shares leapt 15 percent to A$2.22 after Australian billionaire Kerry Packer said his Publishing and Broadcasting had taken a 10 percent stake and bought the casino's management agreement from U.S.-based Showboat Inc for a total of about A$340 million.
Publishing and Broadcasting shares also benefitted from the deal, ending 30 cents higher at A$6.40.
At the smaller end of the market, mineral explorers with interests in the much-touted Gawler Craton gold area in South Australia found plenty of support.
Brokers said the interest appeared linked to the upcoming January 31 deadline for the release of December quarter drilling reports.
Pick of a strong Gawler Craton bunch was area leader, Helix Resources, its shares up 24 percent at a record high of A$4.20.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
